content.text:
I’d replace the Neathacks carousel. It looks like customer endorsement, while the names don’t help visitors understand Hunchlane.

**My preferred replacement:** a quiet, static outcome strip:

**Existing alternatives → Questions worth asking → A small experiment**

Use small teal icons, generous spacing, and no enclosing cards. Keep it horizontal on desktop and stack it on mobile. It bridges the hero’s promise to the sample report below.

Other good options:

- **Remove the strip entirely.** The sample already demonstrates the product; bringing it closer to the hero makes the page tighter.
- **Show one idea’s journey.** A compact example: “Help friends meet” → “Explore scheduling alternatives” → “Try a manual plan.” Label it illustrative. This would need shortening the sample below to avoid repetition.

If you want event attribution, move “Built for Neathacks” and its partner links into the footer.

I reviewed desktop and mobile. The simpler hero and paper illustrations work well. Two fixes should accompany the next UI pass:

- Restore visible keyboard focus in the idea field—the current CSS removes it. [hero.css](/Users/nikhil/Developer/hunchlane/src/app/hero.css:58)
- Increase the send, shuffle, and example controls’ hit areas to the design’s 44px minimum. [hero.css](/Users/nikhil/Developer/hunchlane/src/app/hero.css:64)

No source changes made.
